summary.headline: Flair Q2 FY27 revenue rose 6.5% QoQ to INR340.1 crore, EBITDA margin fell to 14.9%, and FY27 growth guidance was cut to 12%+ after Valsad/Daman floods.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR340.1 crore, up 6.5% QoQ, with exports up 13% QoQ to INR49 crore and domestic sales up 6% QoQ to INR292 crore. Floods in Gujarat shut the Valsad and Daman plants for about 15 and 7 days, costing an estimated INR25 crore of revenue. EBITDA was INR50.6 crore (14.9% margin) and PAT rose 9.1% QoQ to INR31.7 crore (9.3% margin). Management kept FY27 revenue growth guidance at 12%+ and said FY28 onward growth should be about 15%, while flagging higher raw material costs from West Asia and a rise in working capital days to 145.

financial_highlights.change: +11% YoY (from INR513 crore in H1 FY26)
Margin down from 16.7% in Q1 per analyst

segments.name: Writing instruments (Pens)
segments.commentary: Grew 5% in Q2 and 7% in H1 FY27 despite the floods, helped by Uttarakhand, Mumbai outskirts and Daman capacity. Management said Pen volume and value contributed roughly equally to growth; Pen market share is about 18%+.

segments.name: Creative products
segments.commentary: Grew 24% YoY in H1 FY27. Q2 was hit by Valsad disruption, and a new Creative facility is planned in Valsad.

segments.name: Steel bottles and houseware
segments.commentary: Q1 grew about 54% but Q2 was hit by roughly 15 days of Valsad downtime. A fourth steel bottle line is due for commercial operation in Q4 FY27.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance of 12% or higher, cut from about 15% earlier.
Medium-term (FY28 onward) revenue growth target of about 15% YoY reiterated.
EBITDA margin expected to hold around 15% if crude stays at current levels; could return to 16-17% if the global environment improves.
Portfolio mix targeted at 60% pens and 40% non-pens; expected 68:32 by year end per CFO.
Working capital days to be reduced by about 20 days over 5-6 quarters.
Interim dividend of 10% (INR0.50 per share) approved.
Management expects H2 FY27 to be stronger seasonally and with normalised operations.
capex_capacity: Fourth steel bottle line expected to start commercial production in Q4 FY27.
New Creative manufacturing facility planned in Valsad; Creative capacity also being expanded in Surat.
Steel bottles and Creative combined capacity utilisation is about 75%; management said it typically builds new capacity at 70-75%.
Valsad facility to be largely fungible between Creative and Pens.
Management is exploring an acquisition or partnership in the Creative segment; no size or timing disclosed.
demand_pricing: Export demand weakened by West Asia disruption; exports still grew 13% QoQ, with traction in South America, Africa and other Asian markets.
Price increases were taken mainly by cutting discounts and schemes, and new launches are priced at the new input cost. No aggregate price hike figure was given.
Management said new entrants are competing in lower-priced pens and that it operates across mass, mid-premium and premium segments.
Domestic demand described as strong; October numbers not disclosed.
Management said it had been stocking raw materials to take advantage of lower prices; inventory days rose partly for this reason.

qa_highlights.question: How should margins be thought about given raw material volatility and advance stocking?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said the aim is to maintain margins through cost efficiencies and discipline, and the company would keep monitoring volatility. He did not give a split of low-cost inventory or raw material share within INR393 crore inventory.

qa_highlights.question: Was the FY27 growth guidance cut from 15% to 12%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management confirmed the guidance is 12% for FY27, which it said was already set on the last call, and about 15% from FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why were pens less affected by the floods than steel bottles and Creative?
qa_highlights.answer: Pens were supported by other plants in Uttarakhand, Mumbai outskirts and Daman. Steel bottles are made at Valsad, which was down about 15 days.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth needed in H2 and how will it be achieved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to H2 FY26 growth of 17-18%, Creative and steel bottle push, and the Q4 fourth line. It declined to give October numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Will operating leverage or raw material pass-through drive margins as growth accelerates?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said margins are planned at around 15% with a buffer for volatility, and could rise if raw material prices give a benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Why did operating margin fall more than gross margin QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said flood-related costs could not be spread across production in Q2, which is temporary and should reverse in coming quarters. No one-time items were included in other expenses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivables rise and what is the plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Export receivable days rose due to global disruption; domestic receivables were not rising. Target is to cut working capital by about 20 days over 5-6 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Creative acquisition plan and does Flair keep the brand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is open to a partner with a strong manufacturing base; the brand stays with Flair. No size or timing was disclosed.

risks_watch: Raw material cost volatility from West Asia could keep EBITDA margin near 15% or lower.
FY27 guidance needs H2 growth of about 15%, against H1 growth of about 8%.
Working capital days (145) and inventory days (104) remain high; the 20-day reduction target depends on the new ERP and takes 5-6 quarters.
Export receivables and export demand are exposed to West Asia logistics and trade disruption.
Competitive pressure in pens from new lower-priced entrants and peers that are passing on less price increase.
Monsoon and flood risk to Gujarat plants (Valsad and Daman).
Open items: OEM sales and split, pen ASP figures, employee attrition figure in annual report.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth but defensive on the quarter: management attributed the slowdown mainly to floods and geopolitics, and answers on October data, ASP, OEM sales and acquisition size were deferred or withheld.
key_quotes: We are confident that the normalization of operations will support a stronger performance in Q3 and the second half of FY '27.
And if global environment improves, margins will go back to our 16%, 17% range.
So we would not be able to give you the October number.

adds.what: New Creative manufacturing facility in Valsad (fungible with Pens)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 12% or higher (cut from about 15%) with H2 seasonally stronger, backed partly by a fourth steel bottle line due Q4 FY27 and Surat/Valsad Creative capacity, but no quantified order book or capacity size was given and floods cost about INR25 crore of revenue.
